title: Console density token refactor and component composition guidelines
creator: Maya Patel
description: Context: The Redwood Console has accumulated spacing and density variants across cards, metric rows, cost breakdowns, and rollout views. These inconsistencies cause maintenance overhead and subtle layout regressions when runtime shapes change (e.g., long model names, variable token counts in cost UI). Goal: Create a compact-first token set and clear component composition guidelines so teams can safely switch density modes without breaking dashboards or rollout flows. Deliverables: 1) audited token map (spacing, type scale, elevation, container padding, row heights) with mapping to existing token names; 2) Figma library update with compact/regular/comfortable component variants for Card, MetricRow, TableRow, RolloutBanner, CostBreakdownLine; 3) migration guide for engineers with CSS/Token migration snippets and phased rollout plan; 4) small usability prototype (Figma interactive) to validate readability and tap targets at compact density; 5) accessibility checklist for minimum touch targets and contrast at compact sizes. Success criteria: adoption of compact token option by infra/dashboard teams, no visual regressions in top 10 console pages, measured reduction in average vertical space used on high-density dashboards by >=18%.
acceptance_criteria: Token map created and reviewed by design, eng, and docs
Figma library updated and published to org team with version notes
Migration guide with code snippets merged to docs (Confluence/GitHub)
Prototype tested with 5 internal users and feedback captured
No regressions in visual snapshot tests for dashboard & rollouts
steps: Run audit across top console pages to collect current tokens and hard-coded spacing
Create compact-first token naming convention and alias table
Design component variants in Figma and publish library
Coordinate with runtime/product to decide default density for Dedicated and Private consoles
Publish migration guide and schedule cross-team reviews
Partner with QA to add visual snapshots for affected pages
risks: Teams may be slow to adopt new tokens leading to mixed density on pages
Compact token sizes could reduce legibility or fail accessibility thresholds if not validated
Legacy CSS overrides in dashboard repo may require extra engineering effort to purge
